objective: Test one explicitly predeclared past-only volatility gate on lookback-5 momentum through the existing regime-stability and null framework.
observed_effect: The past-only volatility gate (volatility <= 25% annualized) is extremely restrictive for AAPL, blocking all momentum signals because AAPL has historically high volatility (70-120% annualized). Ungated momentum shows REGIME_STABLE behavior (disp=+0.014), but gated momentum produces zero trades and is CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE (disp=+0.000). The gate eliminates the signal rather than improving its robustness.
question: Does a single past-only volatility gate create a predeclared robustness improvement for the qualified momentum effect?
uncertainty_reduced: The test demonstrates that the volatility gate is too restrictive for momentum signals. The same gate that was tested on MA crossover signals is also ineffective for momentum, providing evidence that past-only volatility conditioning with <= 25% annualized threshold cannot be practically applied to momentum strategies on high-volatility assets.
